verdict.rationale: OpenTofu's own CLI covers the plan-and-approve core. `tofu plan` previews changes, speculative plans verify a change before review, and `-out=FILE` saves the plan so `tofu apply` executes only the reviewed plan, giving a natural approval gate. Nothing in the evidence covers agent authoring or agent integration, headless or non-interactive plan flags, or machine-readable plan diff output (the probes found no llms.txt or API). Missing for 10: documented agent-facing workflow, explicit non-interactive/headless plan options, machine-readable plan diff output, hands-on corroboration of an agent-driven plan/approve loop.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent author an infrastructure change, run a plan headlessly, and present the diff for my approval

citations.quote: The `tofu plan` command creates an execution plan, which lets you preview the changes that OpenTofu plans to make to your infrastructure.
developers can use speculative plans to verify the effect of their changes before submitting them for code review
You can use the optional `-out=FILE` option to save the generated plan to a file on disk, which you can later execute by passing the file to `tofu apply` as an extra argument.
